fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point, particularly in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles so responding units can reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Identify and mark any secondary access point to the rear of the property so responders are not limited to a single entry route during an emergency.
• If a gate controls rear access, keep it unlocked or install a Knox-style lock box to allow responders through without delay.
• Trim vegetation growing close to both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move along exterior walls without obstruction.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and the detached structure wide enough for responders carrying equipment.
• Post the detached structure's location on any gate or access point so arriving responders are immediately aware of the second building on the property.
• Keep the area in front of and around the detached structure free of stored materials so responders can work around it without obstruction.
• Confirm that perimeter fencing has at least one operable gate wide enough to allow a responder carrying a hose line or equipment to pass through.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster to create more open space between individual trees and reduce the amount of connected vegetation near the structure.
• Trim any shrubs that are directly touching or within a few feet of the structure's walls, eaves, or vents.
• Cut or mow grass across the open terrain surrounding the structure, particularly during dry periods when grass cures and becomes more flammable.
• Remove dead or dry material from within the irrigated landscape beds closest to the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and any vegetation that could block a vehicle.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate under low visibility or smoky conditions.
• Separate scattered shrubs from one another where they form connected patches between the tree cluster and the structure.
